pathway: Newborn danger signs at a postnatal visit

guideline.name: WHO recommendations on maternal and newborn care for a positive postnatal experience

sourcePassage.section: Executive summary, B. Newborn care, Recommendation 25 (Assessment of the newborn for danger signs)
sourcePassage.quote: The following signs should be assessed during each postnatal care contact, and the newborn should be referred for further evaluation if any of the signs is present: not feeding well; history of convulsions; fast breathing (breathing rate > 60 per minute); severe chest in-drawing; no spontaneous movement; fever (temperature > 37.5 °C); low body temperature (temperature < 35.5 °C); any jaundice in first 24 hours after birth, or yellow palms and soles at any age.

actions.home_care_advice: No danger signs: continue routine postnatal care

inputs.label: Breaths per minute (count for one full minute)
Does the baby move on its own?

openQuestionsForClinician: Exactly 24 hours old with jaundice: is that still 'in the first 24 hours'? Not used as a golden case until a clinician decides.
G14: after 24 hours, is jaundice without yellow palms and soles really not a referral sign? The guideline wording says so; please confirm.
Follow-up after a referral: Recommendation 25 does not say when to follow up, so no golden case expects a follow-up task.
Actions use the team's locked list: 'refer_urgently' stands for 'refer for further evaluation'; 'home_care_advice' stands for 'no danger signs, continue routine postnatal care'.
